page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.4-32 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The server is powered by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor running at a base clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 physical processor cores supporting two threads per core, yielding 8 dedicated vCPUs. System memory is sized at 32.0 GB, resulting in an even memory density of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

Hardware tradeoffs for this instance shape include the complete absence of local disk storage and discrete accelerators. Persistent operations require external network-attached block volumes, as no internal NVMe or SSD drives are bundled. In addition, the instance contains zero GPUs. Dedicated CPU allocation ensures that computational throughput remains consistent, avoiding hypervisor oversubscription or CPU credit degradation common to burstable shapes. Network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The combination of high clock speed Intel processor cores and standard memory density positions this instance well for CPU-bound tasks that do not need specialized accelerator hardware. It is appropriate for mid-tier application hosting, continuous integration and build automation pipelines, batch processing utilities, and relational database services operating against remote network storage.

Given its dedicated core execution, elevated base frequency, and standard compute-to-memory ratio, the shape provides predictable execution suitable for web application tiers, CI/CD automation pipelines, middle-tier enterprise software, and moderate database workloads.
